newsitem.title: USA: Rains, cooler temperatures revive Minnesota crops.
newsitem.headline: Rains, cooler temperatures revive Minnesota crops.

text.p: Rains and cooler weather revived Minnesota's corn and soybean crops in the week ended Sunday and development neared the average pace, said the state's agricultural statistics service.
The crop had been struggling with dry conditions.

Average soybean height as of Sunday was 11 inches, a gain of three inches from last week and equal to the five-year average. Corn height increased 10 inches over the week and reached an average of 33 inches, an inch shorter than average.
Soybeans were rated three percent very poor, 10 percent poor, 38 fair, 42 percent good and seven percent excellent.
Corn was rated two percent very poor, eight percent poor, 31 percent fair, 47 percent good and 12 percent excellent.
Spring wheat was 90 percent jointed, above 86 percent last year but behind the 95 percent average.
Spring wheat was rated three percent very poor, eight percent poor, 47 fair, 32 percent good and 10 percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture was rated one percent very short, five percent short, 63 percent adequate and 31 percent surplus. Last week, soil moisture supplies were 42 percent short to very short.
